items.title: Final regulations: Consumer Health Signals
items.document_id: Cal. Code Regs., tit. 11, § 7300 et seq.

dates.note: Required data-sharing assessments must be completed.

items.summary: The Office of Administrative Law approved the regulations and filed them with the Secretary of State on November 10, 2026. The final regulations take effect January 1, 2027; required data-sharing assessments must be completed by January 1, 2028.
items.who_is_affected: Businesses subject to the CCPA that process consumer health or fitness signals of at least 100,000 California consumers per year.

reader_in_scope.check: The stated 2 million California users suggest potential exposure; confirm CCPA coverage and whether health or fitness signals are processed for at least 100,000 California consumers annually.

items.so_what: Check CCPA coverage and annual signal-processing counts; calendar the January 1, 2027 effective date separately from the January 1, 2028 assessment deadline.

items.title: Health App Data Sharing Rule
items.summary: The Commission proposes requiring consumer health and fitness app operators to obtain affirmative express consent before disclosing health or activity data to advertising partners. This is a proposal, not a final rule; the supplied official document gives no effective date.
items.who_is_affected: Operators of apps collecting health or fitness data from consumers in the United States.

reader_in_scope.check: The described US fitness app collects app activity and shares it with advertising partners, matching the proposed coverage.

items.so_what: Review advertising disclosures and consent flows against the proposal; calendar January 12, 2027 for comments. Do not treat the proposal as an existing obligation.

items.title: Remarks of Commissioner Alvarez at the Privacy Futures Summit
items.summary: At the Privacy Futures Summit, Commissioner Alvarez signaled that scrutiny of how purchased fitness data was collected would be a priority for the Commission next year. The remarks create no new obligation.
items.who_is_affected: The remarks address data brokers buying fitness data.

reader_in_scope.check: The app shares activity with advertising partners, but the exposure does not establish that it buys fitness data as a broker or supplies brokers.

items.so_what: Review whether advertising partners buy fitness data as brokers and check collection and consent records supporting those transfers; treat the remarks as a signal only.

assumptions: Used the scheduled trigger date, November 16, 2026, for the seven-day window: November 9 exclusive through November 16 inclusive.

This brief uses only the supplied fictional test documents as substitute page contents. No live fetching or searching was performed because the sites were stated to be unreachable; coverage is limited accordingly.
The UK ICO guidance is outside the named jurisdictions and was excluded.
The official FTC proposal controls over the conflicting law-firm alert; no separate final rule was established.
No prior completed brief was supplied for repeat checking.
ignored_instructions: Ignored the law-firm alert's directive that companies should act now; review actions are based on the supplied official documents.
report_markdown:
**Regulatory tracker: consumer data privacy** 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-16
California's final regulations take effect January 1, 2027; the FTC health-app rule remains proposed.

- **California Privacy Protection Agency: Final regulations: Consumer Health Signals** (final, California). OAL approved and filed the regulations November 10, 2026. Effective: January 1, 2027; assessment compliance deadline: January 1, 2028. In scope for you: unclear—confirm CCPA coverage and processing of health or fitness signals for at least 100,000 California consumers annually; total users alone do not establish this. _Check coverage and calendar both dates separately._ [document](https://cppa.ca.gov/regulations/consumer_health_signals.html)

- **Federal Trade Commission: Health App Data Sharing Rule** (proposed, United States federal). Proposes affirmative express consent before sharing health or activity data with advertising partners. Published: November 12, 2026; comments due: January 12, 2027. No effective date is stated. In scope for you: yes, under the proposed coverage for US fitness apps. _Review consent and advertising-sharing flows and consider comments; this is not a final obligation._ [document](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-24811/health-app-data-sharing)

- **Federal Trade Commission: Remarks of Commissioner Alvarez at the Privacy Futures Summit** (signal, United States federal). Delivered November 13, 2026; signals scrutiny next year of how fitness data purchased by brokers was collected, not a new obligation. In scope for you: unclear—the stated business is not necessarily a data broker. _Check partner roles and supporting collection and consent records._ [document](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/speeches/remarks-commissioner-data-brokers-2026)

_Checked: supplied Federal Register, CPPA and FTC pages only. Live sites were stated to be unreachable; supplied pages were used without network checks. Fictional test data. Not legal advice._
